what_it_does: This paper describes a chip that acts as a reflective relay for millimeter-wave and sub-terahertz wireless signals (the high-frequency radio waves that power 5G and beyond). When a direct radio path is blocked by walls or obstacles, a relay can bounce the signal to a receiver. The novelty is that this relay measures the angle at which signals arrive and automatically points its output beam toward the receiver—like a satellite that adjusts its antenna aim on the fly. It does this using small antennas built directly onto the chip and avoids lossy signal components (loss means wasted power) that plagued older relay designs. The relay can detect both horizontal (azimuth) and vertical (elevation) angles.
